# Reference

<!-- generated by python/docs_index.py -->

| Page | Summary |
|---|---|
| [data.toml](data-toml.md) | `data.toml` names the datasets a project wants and how to place them. |
| [data.lock](data-lock.md) | `data.lock` pins every selected source file by SHA-256 and size. |
| [Recipes](recipes.md) | a recipe makes a dataset from others with a command of yours; recipes says how fetchloom keys and checks them, and data.toml takes these rules. |
| [Archives](archives.md) | fetchloom unpacks `.zip`, `.7z`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tar.xz`, `.tar.zst`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tgz`, `.txz`, `.tzst`, `.tbz` and `.tbz2`, ignoring case; the bytes choose the decoder. |
| [Environment variables and settings](environment.md) | environment variables choose the cache, network limits, credentials and terminal behavior. |
| [Credentials](credentials.md) | fetchloom reads each source's key where the source's own tools keep it, so a key made for them works here too. |
| [JSON output](json-output.md) | `--json` returns one versioned document on stdout for scripts to read. |
| [Exit codes](exit-codes.md) | exit codes group failures, while error kinds identify the cause. |
| [Python helper](python-helper.md) | install from source with python 3.10 or later and the rust build prerequisites. |
| [Cache folder](cache-folder.md) | the cache is one folder that keeps each file by its SHA-256, with the records fetchloom needs to reuse and check them. |
| [Project folder](project-folder.md) | the project folder holds `data.toml` and `data.lock`, and its `.fetchloom/` holds what this machine knows of the project: a lock, a record of which command holds it, and what sync placed. |
| [Compatibility](compatibility.md) | fetchloom supports the systems, terminals and source APIs listed below. |
| [Limits](limits.md) | fetchloom fetches and pins published inputs; it leaves analysis, publication and data hosting to other systems. |
